0.note: A conclusion was reached and the envelope carries it.

1.note: A negative conclusion, OR an unhandled error escaping as Node's default exit 1. The two are told apart by whether the envelope parses: no envelope means nothing was concluded, which is an infrastructure fault rather than a negative conclusion.

interpreter.positiveEvidence: aggregate.supported + aggregate.supportedWithExceptions > 0 — at least one record actually reached a positive conclusion. This release reports its denominator per record rather than per run, so the run-level evidence question is answered by the aggregate counts. Every count zero means no record was evaluated at all.

knownHazards.hazard: Policy discovery fails OPEN. With no --policy the release walks up to twelve ancestor directories and, finding nothing, falls back to the standards pack's own policy — so a project that adopted nothing can be graded against someone else's rules and produce a real-looking conclusion.
knownHazards.mitigation: --policy is always passed as an absolute path, and the orchestrator stats that file itself before invoking. The release's own discovery is never relied on.

knownHazards.hazard: --policy pointing at a nonexistent file exits 1, not 2, because the load is outside any try/catch. Mapping exit 1 to a negative conclusion would report a missing configuration file as failing work.
knownHazards.mitigation: The policy path is verified before invocation, and exit 1 without a parseable envelope is classified as an infrastructure fault rather than a negative conclusion.

knownHazards.hazard: An omitted target defaults to the release's own example records, and record discovery takes every *.json recursively with no name filter.
knownHazards.mitigation: An absolute target is always passed explicitly.

factSource.derivedFrom: PredictionStandards v1.1.0 (ebe232b): scripts/predictions.mjs, its policy resolution, and a recorded check --json run
